title: One background command's output, as the Shell panel reads it
description: GET /v1/sessions/{id}/shells/{shell}?bytes=N. The Swift app answered this from `Shells.output(of:id:bytes:)` with the same four fields, because `input/shell-panel.js` read them directly. `bytes` is how much of the output file's end to send: 65536 when absent, raised to 1024 and lowered to 1048576 (`sessions.shell_output_bytes`). Only an id the session's transcript announced as a background command is served, whether or not it has ended; any other id, a Codex session, or an announced command whose output file is gone is 404 `not_found`. An id that is not ASCII letters and digits is never looked for.

ShellOutputReply.description: The tail of one command's output file. A reader repaints only when `signature` changes and stops asking once `ended` is true.

shell.description: The command's row, as the session list carries it. `doing` is absent once it has ended.

text.description: The last `bytes` of the output file, starting at a line boundary when the file was longer. UTF-8 as the command wrote it; a byte sequence that is not UTF-8 is replaced.

truncated.description: The file holds more before `text`. Absent when `text` is the whole file.

ended.description: The last non-empty line is Claude Code's ending marker, `[exited …]` or `[killed]`.

signature.description: Changes whenever the file does: its modification time and size.
